ADJOURNED EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  September 23, 2019

An adjourned meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:01 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Brtis, Ciarolla, Silvano, Shinn, Harik, Martin

Committee Members Absent:  Dean-Porter, Zigrang

City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho

DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 20, 2019

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE AUGUST 20, 2019 PARK AND
  ACTIVITES COMMISSION/ EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE

Karina Winje from California Water Service Company distributed project update fact sheets and
highlighted the Palomino Ranchos Trail opening. She described the temporary fencing around
the area of Palomino Ranchos Trail, as the plan is to do intermittent work throughout the fall. MS.
WINJE reported that final intermittent work on the Palomino Rancho Trail will occur during the
day, and may cause temporary trail closures during the work hours. In addition, MS. WINJE
reported that Cal Water Service intends to pave ballfield road and parking lot when all work is
complete.

CHAIR HUFF asked if notices will be sent out when trails are going to be closed.

MS. WINJE responded that Cal Water did not anticipated sending notices, but planned to place
signage on Rolling Hills Road to indicate temporary trail closure. MS. WINJE also noted that
people who live on the trail will still have access to enter and leave because the location of the
work will not affect their trail access.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  1
September 23, 2019
 MEMBER SHINN commented equestrians should be notified. CHAIR HUFF added that the City
could put something on the website and MEMBER SILVANO suggested a Nixle alert be sent to
inform the equestrian community of all of all work and closures.

MS. WINJE responded that Cal Water will work on providing notice to residents for additional
closures and that they are pushing the contractor to finish work in a timely manner.

MEMBER SHINN asked if trails will be closed the part of the time. MS. WINJE affirmed.

MEMBER SHINN asked if the trail closed for two or three days or a few hours a day. MS. WINJE
responded the trail was closed part of the time, with some people getting through.

MEMBER BRTIS commented that it is not clear when the trails are closed and has had residents
approach her with questions on the closure times.

MS. WINJE responded that it is hard from Cal Water’s perspective because they are working
under a time constraint and do the best to work within the time allowed.

MEMBER SILVANO commented the work should not get held up because of notification and we
should allow them to work to get everything done. MEMBER HARIK commented that detour signs
work well.

MS. WINJE stated the Botanic Trail is open from Blossoms Trail west through the tunnel. The
section from Blossoms Trail to Lariat Lane will be open in October; work is progressing. There
has been some work around special trees within the Botanic Garden. MEMBER BRITIS asked,
are planting is expected in October. MS. WINJE affirmed that CalWater has planting on the
punch list for the Palomino Rancho Trail.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF THANKED MS. WINJE AND RECEIVED AND FILED
THE REPORT.

2019 CITY CELEBRATION EQUESTRIAN EVENTS DEBRIEFING

MEMBER SHINN reported that the drill teams were fabulous and things went really well overall;
however, there was some difficulty in coordinating the equestrian games with the music
performance.

CHAIR HUFF asked what time the band start and if it could be adjusted. MEMBER SHINN
responded that the band began at 11:00 am and the games were delayed because people
showed up late. The Symphonic Band and equestrian games took a break from 12-1 pm due to
Mayor’s Speech. Equestrian games and band restarted at 12:30 pm. MEMBER SILVANO added
that events were still able to be coordinated and only Musical Poles game was delayed.

CHAIR HUFF suggested that maybe the band play a little less.

MEMBER MARTIN added it was difficult to work around the schedule in coordination with the
music. In addition, the DJ was also finding it difficult to work around the equestrian schedule and
the Band performance. MEMBER MARTIN also added a lot of the kids’ stuff was on one side of
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  2
September 23, 2019
 the club, MEMBER MARTIN suggested adding more games where the band was playing and
consider having the DJ play the entire time.

MEMBER SHINN commented that last year the stick horse rodeo was held in the grass area,
where it was easier for the kids to run. She further explained that they were unable to host the
stick horse rodeo in the grass area this year due to the band. MEMBER MARTIN added that the
area might have been better used for more kid’s games to help balance out the space. He also
expressed that the saddle stands, pony rides and all kids area were well attended.

MEMBER HARIK commented that she observed more children in the Corn Pit than in the Hay pit
and suggested we provide two Corn Pits and eliminate the hay pit. MEMBER SHINN responded
that last year it was suggested that there be two Corn Pits as that is usually the hit of the event.
MEMBER SILVANO added that the City makes the Corn Pit and it would be more beneficial to
have two pits. MEMBER CIAROLLA commented that she observed some kids playing the Hay
pit.

MEMBER MARTIN suggested possibly charging more for tickets and bracelets to help offset cost
of event. With the purchase of one wrist band at $12, people were taking advantage and going
on pony rides constantly.

MEMBER SHINN recommended not charging for any equestrian games or making it less
expensive by selling a wrist band for participation in all events. MEMBER SILVANO responded
to consider only selling wrist bands. MEMBER BRTIS agreed explaining that having only a wrist
band for equestrian games would be helpful in coordinating. MEMBER MARTIN added that $5.00
would be a good price for a wrist band and stated that everyone participating knows it is for charity
and is willing to pay.

MEMBER HARIK commented the turn out for the poker ride was great. MEMBER MARTIN added
the turn out might have been the same as last year. The poker ride handed out about 140 hands.
MEMBER SILVANO commented that Melody Colbert is no longer active in PVP Horsemens
Association and for that reason, not many poker ride prizes were collected early on in the planning
process. MEMBER CIAROLLA mentioned that there were poker ride prizes in the end. MEMBER
MARTIN added that Ms. Colbert has collected prizes for so long and her moving out was a difficult
transition. MEMBER SILVANO added that the week before the event there had only been seven
prizes collected.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO how many prizes the PVPHA
collected. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO responded that the City sent out donation request
letters on behalf of the PVPHA and assisted in collecting and inventorying donated prizes.
SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO also added that going into the week of the event, seven prizes
had been collected. She further explained that staff reached out to the PVPHA and Equestrian
Committee to help solicit additional prizes for the event. MEMBER MARTIN added that in the
past Andy Clark would mail out letters and Melody Colbert would follow up with a phone call to
verify that the letter was received.

MEMBER SHINN asked what the best solution to address prize donations is. MEMBER SILVANO
responded that the Poker Ride is a PVPHA event and they are in responsible for coordinating
prizes as they receive 50% of the proceeds. The City supports the event by sending out letters
to vendors for donation. She further explained that Ms. Colbert in the past was able to collect up
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  3
September 23, 2019
 to 50 prizes. MEMBER MARTIN suggested approaching vendors for donation on Poker Ride up
to 3 months in advance.

MEMBER CIAROLLA suggested that City staff and Equestrian committee also help more in
finding prizes since 50% of the funds raised will be received by the Pepper Tree Foundation.

MEMBER SHINN suggested another area of improvement is the sign-up sheets for equestrian
trail classes. She explained that in previous years, carbon copy paper was used for sign ups, this
year everything was done by hand and the process took longer to announce winners. MEMBER
SILVANO added, that carbon copy paper is expensive and sign-ups can be done with better
planning. She suggested that if sign-up sheets were separated by age categories, it would help
to determine who is signed up and for what classes.

MEMBER BRTIS commented that carbon copy sheets are not needed, but should have a list to
add names for each age group, so that it can be referenced throughout the day. She also
explained that it might also help to have three different color wrist bands for age categories.
MEMBER HARIK suggested letting people sign up under the classes they wanted to participant
in.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if there are liability forms available at the event. MEMBER HARIK
responded that forms are onsite and must be signed by participant or parent of participant if under
18.

The EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE commended MEMBER MARTIN on getting so many people to
sign up and participate in the Equestrian Trail Classes and commented on how well the drill teams
performed.

MEMBER MARTIN suggested that there might be an opportunity to host equestrian event longer
for attendees who are not available in the morning to participate. MEMBER SHINN commented
that adding an evening BBQ and country western band would be a good addition to the event.
MEMBER SILVANO responded that it may be too long of a day if afternoon activities are added.

CHAIR HUFF commented that the food served at City Celebration was minimal and stated that .
the food vendor ran out of condiments and in the past they served a salad but this year there was
only hamburgers, chips and a drink.

MEMBER CIAROLLA mentioned that a BBQ lunch was something that was done in the past and
it should be considered to be brought back again. MEMBER SILVANO commented that the food
is Empty Saddle Club’s responsibility and suggested we discuss the food menu with them.

MEMBER HARIK commented that Empty Saddle Club could still run their bar, but it should be
considered that outside vendor come in to sell food, or Empty Saddle Club change their menu.
MEMBER SILVANO responded it may be a concern to be responsible for the food and it helps
that the Empty Saddle Club to organize food sales. MEMBER SHINN commented it is important
to have good quality food available during the event. MEMBER MARTIN suggested bringing in
outside food vendors or city volunteers barbeque.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  4
September 23, 2019
 CHAIR HUFF commented that at last year’s debrief it was suggested that canopies be used for
shade during the event. MEMBER HARIK added some easy ups would help as it was too hot to
sit in the picnic area without shade.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if the City is charged to use the Empty Saddle Club. MEMBER
MARTIN affirmed. MEMBER SILVANO responded that it may be possible that the Empty Saddle
Club might raise their fee if the City does not allow them to sell food during the event. CHAIR
HUFF commented maybe they can enhance their food options. MEMBER MARTIN suggested
reaching out to Empty Saddle Club to see if additional food vendors would be allowed with a
percentage going to Empty Saddle Club. In this case, the City can control the food quality and
Empty Saddle Club can still receive funds. MEMBER HARIK responded that Empty Saddle Club
could still be responsible for the bar area.

CHAIR HUFF thanked the Equestrian Committee and congratulated them on a successful event.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO reported that issues listed in the published log have been
addressed accordingly.

MEMBER CIAROLLA commented that in the past carts have been allowed on trails. MEMBER
CIAROLLA asked why this issue was raided and if carts are allowed on the trails.

MEMBER SILVANO responded it was more about how they were operating the cart that was the
concern.

MEMBER SHINN added there are a couple of issues including the concern that the driver and
horses are not trained to pull a cart. MEMBER CIAROLLA agreed that is a completely different
concern. MEMBER SHINN added the driver of the carriage could not stop when necessary and
stated that the City has been notified of the issue and signage does allow for carts and carriages
on trails. MEMBER SHINN requested that staff provide more information at the next equestrian
meeting on the rules and regulations of carts and carriages on City trails.

MEMBER CIAROLLA responded in the past that carts and carriages were allowed on trails and
there was a carriage race on the trails.

AUDIENCE MEMBER BECKY MARTIN added there is a difference between carriages and the
carts further explaining that the amount of momentum is different with the horses pulling a larger
carriage versus a horse pulling a smaller cart.

MEMBER SHINN suggested agendizing the issue for a future meeting.

MEMBER SILVANO responded that the Committee cannot become exclusionary for what is
permitted on the trails. MEMBER SHINN added if it is a safety issue it should be reviewed and
discussed. MEMBER SILVANO responded that the cart is no longer being used since they have
been contacted by the City. MEMBER SHINN added that Assistant City Manager is looking into
the issue as well.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  5
September 23, 2019
 CHAIR HUFF asked if are there any other issues.

MEMBER MARTIN reported that a man has been seen on several occasions on a bike near the
ballfield trail entrance hanging out in the bushes. The man followed residents on bike and after
the resident addressed the man and asked if he need to pass, the man ran off. He further reported
that the resident stated that he was acting kind of weird; however the Sheriff’s Department station
has not been contacted. MEMBER HARIK asked what kind of bike. MEMBER MARTIN
responded a mountain bike, which are not allowed on the trails. MEMBER CIAROLLA mentioned
she has encountered a similar issue with seeing bikes on the trails. MEMBER SHINN suggested
contacting the Sheriff’s Department about the issue.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A- TRAIL – No Updates provided.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

MEMBER SHINN requested the following items be brought as future items.

  •  ADDRESS ENCLOSURES DURING HORSE SHOWS AT ERNIE HOWLETT
  PARK

  •  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE

  •  CARRIAGES AND CARTS ON TRAILS

  •  HORSE CENSUS

CHAIR HUFF asked anyone had any other comments. AUDIENCE MEMBER BECKY MARTIN
responded, September 22, 2019 she hosted her event and wanted to thank the Committee and
the City for allowing them to use the Ernie Howlett Facility.

ADJOURNMENT

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER CIAROLLA

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:47 p.m

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  6
September 23, 2019
 Respectfully submitted,

Cynthia Morquecho
Community Services Supervisor

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  7
September 23, 2019
